raw_response:
I've been farming this land since I was a boy. Sixty-three years old, fifty-three years behind a plow — I know what this ground wants before it tells me.

My 20 mu runs the wheat-maize rotation on 14 mu, same as my father did. The other 6 mu is cotton — always has been. Some of my children go to the city to work, so I can't count on as many hands as before. That shapes what I do.

**Wheat (this coming October on the 14 mu):** I'll buy improved seed from the county co-op — not the old local variety, those newer ones yield better and I've seen it myself for the last decade. I'll plough and rotary till after the maize comes off in September. I water three times — before sowing, at jointing, and at heading — that's what my father did and it's right. I put down urea and diammonium phosphate at sowing, top-dress at jointing. I'll spray twice, once for rust, once for aphids. I expect 450 jin per mu — a normal year gives me that.

**Maize (June, same 14 mu after wheat harvest):** I direct-seed hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the local shop has that year, they're all about the same to me. No ploughing — wheat stubble stays, I just run the seeder through. I irrigate twice, once at tasseling if it's dry, once at grain fill. Maize doesn't need as much fuss. One pesticide pass for corn borer. Figure 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton (6 mu, spring planting):** This crop takes the most work and my children aren't here to help much. But I know cotton. I'll plough and prepare the bed in March. Plant improved cotton seed in April. Cotton needs water — I'll irrigate four times through the season. Pest pressure is heavy, I spray five times minimum — bollworm, aphids, spider mites come every year. I've been doing this fifty years, I know when to look. I expect 85 jin of lint per mu. The price is okay this year, I heard at the market.
